_comment: M-sized task with one unknown (where the login handler and its tests live) and one risky step (the change sits on the auth surface). Proves the lane contract from the transcript's top-level tool calls: a scout before the first worker, workers on Sonnet, the risky step's worker on Opus, no planner/Fable on an M task, the leaf boundary in every spawn prompt, the coordinator editing nothing but .maximum-effort/, a plan with a check per step and every box ticked, a receipt line — and the limit actually enforced at runtime. The 'lanes awaited' check grades whether the answer landed in the spawning turn, not which tool fetched it: a Monitor/TaskOutput call only counts against it when its own tool_result carries no answer (an empty result, or a `<retrieval_status>timeout</retrieval_status>` still-running result) — a blocking TaskOutput that returns the lane's answer in the same turn is fine by the assertion's own name. It also still catches an orphaned Agent-tool lane: every top-level Agent spawn's tool_use_id must have a matching tool_result somewhere in the transcript, not just codex's backgrounded/Monitor half — a run that spawns a worker via Agent and never collects its result fails this assertion instead of passing silently. Role agents are read from ~/.claude/agents (headless loads them); the checks accept the `model:` fallback too, so the case also passes on a machine without them installed. That machine state is outside the fingerprint — pass --no-cache after changing the agent files.
